results.resolution: Move the trailhead pin from the crag to the dead end of the left-fork spur of FS 9070 below Silver Basin, where two independent road datasets end the road within ~25 m of each other; set its elevation to the ground there.
results.summary: The trailhead pin sat on the crag itself; it now sits at the road-end turnaround below Silver Basin, about 650 m north of the buttress.
results.evidence: The route and its area both say: take the left fork of FS 9070 past Olallie Meadow to a large turnaround just below Silver Basin, then walk 20-30 min to the wall. The crag's own published position is 47.36741,-121.45564 (the Sofa King Buttress area), which is exactly where the trailhead pin sat - so pin 0 was a copy of the crag coordinate, and its 4585 ft is the parent area's elevation. Two independent road datasets map the west-running left-fork spur (leaving 9070 at ~47.3748,-121.4483) to a single dead end below the basin: the U.S. Forest Service road layer (USFS Roads 11/2019, served by the National Map transportation service, objectids 8644136 + 30672049) ends it at 47.37289,-121.45781, and OpenStreetMap's 9070-310 track (traced from imagery) ends it at 47.37310,-121.45793 - about 25 m apart. The earlier pass's second OSM spur end (47.37239,-121.45690) is a short side track ~100 m away that the USFS layer does not have. The USFS Silver Peak trail (#1300) starts at 47.36684,-121.45554, right below the crag, consistent with a walk up into the basin from this road end. Ground at the new point is ~4,254 ft (USGS 1 m DEM); the crag pin's 4,650 ft is consistent with ground ~4,668 ft there. The crag pin [1] is correct and unchanged. Sibling rows wa_spraying_mantis[0] carries the same wrong trailhead coordinate (not in this task). No distance or gain changed.

results.resolution: Move the Alta turnoff pin onto the mapped fork where the Alta climbers' path leaves the Lila Lake trail, and (found on the way, same sources) move the Rampart Ridge junction pin onto the mapped ridge-top junction, which it missed by ~400 m; drop the 'estimate / interpolation' sentences from both notes; set the turnoff elevation to the ground.
results.summary: The cairned turnoff pin now sits on the actual fork on the Lila Lake trail, and the ridge-top junction pin, which sat down toward the Rampart Lakes basin, now sits on the junction itself.
results.evidence: Turnoff: OpenStreetMap maps the Lila Lake trail (#1313.1) from the Rampart Ridge junction (47.42417,-121.33388) to a node at 47.42786,-121.33165 where a separate informal 'Alta Mountain Trail' branches north and ends at the summit (47.44101,-121.33193, a few m from the summit pin). Independently recorded public GPS tracks of Alta ascents by different users in different years (2015, 2024, 2025, 2026; 11 downloadable GPX files checked) all pass within 1-4 m of that fork and turn north/northwest up the ridge there, and those that summit reach it within ~6-12 m of the summit pin. The old pin (47.4285,-121.3332, labelled an estimate) was ~80 m NW of the fork, up on the climbers' path. Ground at the fork is ~5,237 ft (USGS 1 m DEM). Ridge junction (pin 2, not in the original ask but on the same line and settled by the same sources): OpenStreetMap and the U.S. Forest Service trail layer (Lila Lake #1313.1 begins at 47.42421,-121.33398) put the junction at the same spot within ~10 m, and the recorded tracks pass within 1-7 m of it; the pin at 47.42,-121.334 was ~400 m south of every track, toward the Rampart Lakes basin. Its stated 5,100 ft matches the ground at the junction (~5,122 ft), so the elevation is kept. The drawn line on the row is the published route line that follows these trails through both points, so it needs no change. No distances or gains changed.

results.resolution: No change. The tower's base and top-out pins are certainly misplaced, but no two sources give the tower's position, and the pins are not provably more than 500 m from the route's own line (they may sit on the lower approach wash), so rule 1 does not allow removal.
results.summary: The base and top-out pins sit on ground about 2,000 ft lower than they claim and east of where the tower is, but nothing published gives the tower's position twice, so they are left for the owner.
results.evidence: Live pins: [1] 'Dolomite Tower Base' 47.7805,-121.429 (claims 5,200 ft; ground ~3,327 ft) and [2] 'Vanishing Point Topout' 47.781,-121.430 (claims 5,708 ft; ground ~3,351 ft); [3] 'Dolomite Tower' 47.77918,-121.43599 is the Baring Mountain main summit (OSM/GNIS peak 47.77928,-121.43583; ground ~6,074 ft) and is also the only coordinate any climbing page publishes for the tower (the area page and the route page both use it). New this pass: (a) a first-hand descent description places the tower NORTH of the main summit, separated from it by a notch ('the notch separating you from the highest peak, which is to the south'), with the descent going west from that col, down ~700 ft of boulders and meadow, then to the low point of the west ridge; (b) a public recorded GPS track titled 'Vp approach' (2026-08-13) goes up the west-ridge trail to that ridge low point (~47.7789,-121.4448, ~4,800 ft) and then traverses east to end at 47.78173,-121.43961 (~4,900 ft), i.e. WNW of the main summit - the reverse of that descent; (c) OSM maps the north-face cliff from 47.7779,-121.4363 to 47.7816,-121.4393. Together these put the tower just NW/N of the main summit around longitude -121.436 to -121.440, and the approach wash leaving the Barclay Lake trail before the removed bridge (OSM 47.78856,-121.43875) and climbing south beneath the north face. The two pins are ~400-500 m east of that corridor and ~1,000-2,000 ft below their stated heights, so they are wrong, but (1) the track ends ~800 ft below the tower top and at neither the base nor the top-out, so it cannot place either pin, and it is the only coordinate source for the tower; (2) the lower wash's exact course is not published, so the pins cannot be shown to be >500 m from the route's own line. Recommend the owner either accept a single-source placement or remove pins 1 and 2 (leaving trailhead + summit), since both mislead as they stand.

results.resolution: Rule 1: remove the 'Blood Sport crag' pin. It is a copy of the peak-wide coordinate, ~150 m from Guye Peak's summit and ~800 ft above the crag's stated height, while every description puts this 50-ft crag low at the base of the South Rib, a short walk from the road; no source publishes the crag's own position, so it cannot be moved. The trailhead and summit pins are kept.
results.summary: The crag pin sat next to Guye Peak's summit, far above a small roadside crag at the foot of the South Rib, and nothing publishes where the crag actually is, so the pin is removed rather than left pointing climbers up the mountain.
results.evidence: Live pin [1] 'Blood Sport crag' 47.442,-121.411 (elev 3,400) is exactly the peak-wide coordinate used for Guye Peak; ground there is ~4,227 ft and it is ~150 m from the OSM 'Guye Peak' (south) summit node 47.44198,-121.40891 and the route's own summit pin 47.4415,-121.4093. The route page describes an isolated crag 'down low' near the BASE of the South Rib, just around the corner right of the large west face, visible from the west-most Summit West parking lots (at the pass, south of the peak), with a single 50-ft pitch, no top-out, and a ~15-minute walk; the row's own face/overview/note agree ('low on the mountain', 'at the base of the South Rib'). The South Rib itself is a 7-pitch-plus climb (a pitch or two of 4th class, then gullies and four or five 70-ft rock steps) from its base to the south summit block, so its base - and the crag - lies well south of and far below the summit, while the route never climbs above the 50-ft crag. The pin therefore marks the top of the mountain, a place the route never goes, more than 500 m from the crag at the rib's foot. The route's published GPS (47.44195,-121.40882) is the shared coordinate of the whole 'Summer-Fall (rock)' sub-area (the South Rib route page carries the identical value), so it does not locate the crag; no other source gives a coordinate. Removing it leaves the trailhead and the summit pin. Follow-up for the owner (not written): the summit pin is also not on this route's line, and the trailhead note's 'traverse east along the base of the south rib' from the Alpental lot deserves a check against 'visible from the Summit West lots'.
